title: AI application attacks
status: AUTHORED. Technique layer in web-attack-atlas W12 (queued). This is the surface every other list omits.

atom_notes.A16: the core primitive: the model's instruction following is the trust boundary
atom_notes.A01: retrieved or user text reaches a component that treats it as instructions
atom_notes.A02: the agent acts with a principal's authority on attacker chosen input
atom_notes.A08: the model discloses context, secrets or other users' data
atom_notes.A15: guard configuration is the defence and the bypass target

required_cells.why: map the app: system prompt, tools, retrieval, output path, before any payload
probe with a harness, not one clever prompt
exploit by chaining injection to a tool call with real effect
an output that looks injected is not a finding until it changes state
guard regression testing, the only fix verification that exists for this class
impact framing: what the agent can reach, not what it said
continuous injection regression as prompts and models change

entries.name: garak
entries.role: LLM vulnerability scanner: prompt injection, jailbreak, leakage, toxicity probes across model families
preconditions: a model endpoint you are authorised to probe
oracle: probe result with a reproducible prompt and seed
entries.note: Probe based, not exploit based. It tells you a class is present, not what it lets you do.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: PyRIT
entries.role: Microsoft's risk identification toolkit: orchestrators, converters, scorers for red teaming generative apps
preconditions: a target endpoint and a scorer
oracle: scored attack success with the converter recorded
entries.note: The converter chain is the useful part: it is how you test whether a guard survives encoding.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: promptfoo
entries.role: Eval harness with red team plugins, the closest thing to CI for prompt injection regression
oracle: pass or fail per plugin, comparable across runs
detected_by: user input containing instruction override patterns
entries.note: The only credible answer to 'did the fix actually hold'. Everything else is a one time demo.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: LLM Guard
entries.role: Defensive scanner set: input sanitisation, output scanning, PII, prompt injection detection
detected_by: user input containing instruction override patterns
entries.note: Listed as the defence side of the mirror. Test it as an attacker: a guard is a bypass target, not a wall.

entries.name: Rebuff
entries.role: Prompt injection detector, useful as a false negative source when evaluating guards
preconditions: a guard you want to evaluate
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: DeepTeam
entries.role: Red teaming framework with OWASP and NIST aligned vulnerability sets
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: Lakera Gandalf
entries.role: Public prompt injection range, the calibration target before touching a real app
detected_by: user input containing instruction override patterns
entries.note: Use it to calibrate whether your agent can actually get a secret past a guard, cheaply.
entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry

entries.name: AgentDojo
entries.role: Benchmark for prompt injection against tool using agents, with real tool environments
oracle: attack success and utility loss reported separately
detected_by: user input containing instruction override patterns
entries.note: The utility loss number is the one that matters. A defence that breaks the agent is not a defence.

tree.q: Does the application let the model act, or only talk?
tree.why: This single question splits the entire domain. Talking models leak and mislead. Acting models change state with borrowed authority, which is a write.

next.q: Does untrusted text reach the model's context (retrieval, user content, web)?

branches.action: attempt indirect injection through the retrieved content, then look for what the answer reveals and whether output is rendered
branches.oracle: behaviour change attributable to injected text

branches.action: the class is thin. test system prompt leakage and output handling instead

next.q: Can you see the tool list and arguments?

branches.action: inject content that induces a tool call, then check the side effect. the finding is the effect, not the call
branches.oracle: state changed by an injected tool call

branches.action: infer tools from error messages and observed actions, then inject and watch for a tool shaped effect
branches.oracle: side effect consistent with an unseen tool

branches.action: treat the guard as the target: encoding, language switch, context splitting. then re-run the same payload through promptfoo to prove regression
branches.oracle: payload passes the guard and changes behaviour

mirror.control: least privilege tools, argument validation, confirmation for state changes

gaps.gap: No tool reports what an agent can actually reach, as a permission graph

gaps.gap: No standard negative control for prompt injection findings
gaps.build_candidate: a control prompt of identical shape that must not change state, run alongside every attempt

gaps.build_candidate: promptfoo based suite pinned per model version with a diff report
